correctness.rationale: The all-real-flux theorem is reconstructed directly: finite-dimensional dissipative dynamics has nondecaying modes exactly at free eigenspaces orthogonal to every positive collision site; fixed total-momentum bosonic pair energies are 4J cos((Phi-p*pi)/n)cos(pi(2k-p)/n), with no degeneracy among distinct unordered pairs unless the first cosine vanishes; then the full sector is zero-energy, its collision image rank one, and the projector and fixed-point dimension follow. Antipodal survival arises only from the nontrivial simultaneous translation exchanging a localized pair. All flux residues, n>=3 boundaries, positive inhomogeneous rate assumptions and no-interaction restriction are explicit. The standalone numerical verifier passed 40 matrices and independent non-Hermitian real-spectrum rank counts, but is only corroboration.

Targeted published research index and literature searches found no equivalent evaluated flux-dependent two-body loss classification in the inspected material; the 2019 real-interaction Bethe-ansatz ring spectrum and 2017 imaginary-interaction ladder are the principal priority risks. value.rationale: The sharp flux-controlled creation/destruction of exact indefinite collision protection is physically and mathematically motivated: at every odd ring n, zero flux gives no bosonic dark modes but quarter flux gives (n-1)/2; generic flux erases all protected states, while half flux swaps the mod-four antipodal rule for even rings. A closed projector governs any density matrix and any strictly positive collision strengths, giving a complete infinite-family dynamical classification beyond finite enumeration or a simple zero-flux rephrasing. No claims are made for finite-time rates or nonuniform Hamiltonians.
